objectives: Name and describe the three types of rock
Explain physical, chemical and biological weathering
Describe the soil profile and the main soil types

blocks.md: **Rocks** make up the Earth's crust. There are three main types. **Igneous** rocks form when hot liquid rock (magma, or lava at the surface) cools and hardens, for example **granite** and **basalt**. **Sedimentary** rocks form when sand, mud and shells are laid down in layers and pressed together, for example **sandstone** and **limestone**. **Metamorphic** rocks are older rocks changed by great heat or pressure, for example **marble** (from limestone) and **slate** (from shale).

blocks.caption: A soil profile
blocks.alt: Four horizontal layers from topsoil down to bedrock.

blocks.title: Weathering
blocks.md: **Weathering** is the breaking down of rocks where they lie, without movement by water or wind. **Physical** weathering: heating by day and cooling at night makes the rock crack and flake. **Chemical** weathering: rain water, which is slightly acid, slowly changes minerals; limestone dissolves. **Biological** weathering: roots grow into cracks and widen them.

Weathered rock, mixed with dead plants and animals (**humus**), forms **soil**. A vertical cut through the soil is a **soil profile**. At the top is the dark **topsoil** rich in humus; below is the **subsoil**; then partly weathered rock; at the bottom is solid **bedrock**. Soil particles are **sand** (large), **silt** and **clay** (very small). A mixture of the three, called **loam**, is good for farming.

blocks.title: Soils near us
blocks.md: Around **Mount Cameroon** the soils come from volcanic rock and are fertile, which is why bananas, oil palm and rubber are grown there. In many tropical lands heavy rain washes out plant foods and leaves a red soil rich in iron, often called **laterite**; it can be poor for crops unless it is well managed.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Weathering is not erosion: in weathering the rock breaks where it is; in erosion the pieces are carried away.
- Marble and slate are metamorphic, not igneous.
- Fertile soil is not only a matter of colour: it needs humus, minerals and water.

blocks.title: Example 1: classify the rock
blocks.statement: A rock is made of tiny shells pressed into layers and contains fossils. What type is it, and what could it be called?
steps: Layers and fossils show a sedimentary rock.
Rock made of shells is limestone.
So it is a sedimentary rock such as limestone.

blocks.title: Example 2: the type of weathering
blocks.statement: In a dry region a rock splits after many hot days and cold nights. Which type of weathering is this, and why?
steps: The rock heats by day and cools by night.
The change makes the surface expand and contract and crack.

parts.prompt: Which layer of the soil profile contains most humus?
parts.explanation: Humus is concentrated at the surface.

parts.prompt: Give two ways to keep a soil fertile.
parts.model: Add manure or compost, rotate crops, plant cover crops and avoid bare soil; also use terraces on slopes.
